name: Nexus Data Centers
desc: Develops hyperscale data center campuses for AI workloads, led by a planned gas-powered campus near Hubbard, Texas.
markets: Campus development in Texas only; pre-revenue developer with no verified operations or expansion plans outside the United States.
rationale: Pre-revenue Texas data-centre developer with no consumer brand; B2B hospitality for hyperscale tenants is the only angle, weak F1 fit.
changed: Transition Equity Partners made a strategic equity investment in December 2025

name: Project Prometheus
desc: Early-stage startup co-led by Jeff Bezos building AI for engineering and manufacturing in computers, aerospace and automobiles.
markets: Pre-revenue; team and facilities in the US San Francisco Bay Area only; no disclosed customers or international operations.
rationale: Bezos-led AI for automotive and aerospace engineering has a technology story, but it is pre-revenue and secretive; weak F1 fit now.

name: Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust
desc: Owns and leases more than 258,000 telecom towers and sites across India to mobile network operators.
markets: Towers and tenants in India only; no verified operations or expansion plans outside India.
rationale: Domestic B2B tower owner with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship offers little commercial return.
changed: Renamed Altius in 2024; absorbed American Tower's India tower business; La Caisse agreed to buy a 24% stake in September 2026

name: Atoms
desc: Travis Kalanick's group running CloudKitchens facilities, Otter restaurant software and Pronto autonomous haulage for mining.
markets: 90+ US kitchen facilities; Otter software used in 40+ countries; mining deployments on three continents; Latin America, Australia, Asia targeted.
rationale: Heavily funded, high-profile Kalanick company spanning food, mining and transport automation; F1 could showcase robotics to industrial partners.
changed: Formerly City Storage Systems (CloudKitchens); emerged as Atoms in 2026, unifying food, mining and transport businesses

name: Bitfarms
desc: Operates bitcoin mining data centers in Canada and the United States and is converting sites to AI computing.
markets: Sites in Quebec, Canada and Pennsylvania and Washington, US; earlier Argentina and Paraguay operations not confirmed as current.
rationale: North American crypto miner pivoting to AI hosting with little consumer awareness; weak F1 fit beyond investor visibility.
changed: Announced 2026 redomicile to the US and rename to Keel Infrastructure (ticker KEEL, Nasdaq and TSX); completion not confirmed

name: Crusoe
desc: Builds and operates AI data center campuses and rents GPU cloud capacity to AI labs and enterprises.
industry: AI data centers and GPU cloud
markets: Campuses in Texas, Wyoming and other US states; data centers in Norway and Iceland serving Crusoe Cloud customers.
rationale: High-profile AI infrastructure builder for Microsoft and OpenAI-linked projects; F1 offers technology storytelling and B2B hospitality.

name: Hyperliquid Strategies
desc: Nasdaq-listed digital asset treasury company that holds and stakes HYPE tokens of the Hyperliquid blockchain.
markets: US-listed holding vehicle with no customers; income depends on HYPE token value and staking rewards.
rationale: Token treasury vehicle with no products or customers to market; very weak F1 fit.
changed: Formed through business combination with Sonnet BioTherapeutics; began trading on Nasdaq in December 2025

name: Avalon Labs
desc: Bitcoin-focused lending platform offering bitcoin-backed loans, the USDa stablecoin, yield accounts and a credit card.
markets: Online protocol on 20+ blockchains; customer countries not disclosed; no verified offices or licensed operations outside its base.
rationale: Crypto lenders such as OKX and Nexo already sponsor F1, but Avalon is small and offshore; plausible only as a niche crypto deal.

name: Axiom Solutions International
desc: Private company reported to make digital and electrical infrastructure for AI data centers, cloud computing, utilities and industry.
markets: Only an aggregator profile found; customer markets and any operations outside the United States are not verified.
rationale: Little verified public information; a B2B electrical supplier to data centers with no evident brand marketing, weak F1 fit until confirmed.

name: Fireworks AI
desc: Runs an inference platform serving open-source and custom AI models to developers and enterprises through APIs and fine-tuning.
markets: Mainly US customers such as Uber, Shopify and Cursor; infrastructure in Frankfurt, Iceland and Tokyo; customers include Samsung and Heidi Health.
rationale: Fast-growing AI inference brand whose rivals Groq and CoreWeave sponsor F1; technology showcase and enterprise hospitality could suit it.

name: Joulent
desc: Develops multi-gigawatt gas-fired power plants co-located with large data centers, with Microsoft reported as an initial offtaker.
markets: Power projects for US data centers only; pre-revenue development portfolio with no verified international plans.
rationale: New Houston power developer selling to hyperscalers, with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond B2B hospitality.
changed: Launched in 2026 by Engine No. 1; National Grid Ventures agreed to invest for a 35% stake

name: SK Horizon
desc: SK Telecom company formed to operate SK Broadband's data centers and submarine cables and build AI data centers in Korea.
markets: Eight operating data centers in Seoul region and Busan plus AI sites under construction in Ulsan and Guro; Korea only.
rationale: Domestic B2B infrastructure unit with no consumer brand; parent SK Telecom has more marketing reach, but SK Horizon itself is a weak fit.
changed: Spin-off from SK Broadband announced August 2026 with KKR and IMM investment; expected to complete in 2027

name: Flapping Airplanes
desc: AI research lab working on data-efficient model training, focused on fundamental research and not yet selling products.
markets: Pre-revenue research lab in the United States; no customers, products or international operations disclosed.
rationale: Research-stage lab with no product or brand to market; weak F1 fit.

name: SandboxAQ
desc: Sells AI and quantum-based software for drug discovery, post-quantum cybersecurity and quantum navigation to enterprises and governments.
markets: US enterprise and defence customers; UK National Cyber Security Centre; Bahrain government contracts; staff in Canada, UK, France and Spain.
rationale: Well-funded deep-tech brand selling to governments and enterprises across regions; F1 offers technology storytelling and B2B hospitality.

name: Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI Labs)
desc: AI start-up led by Yann LeCun developing world models for robotics, healthcare and industry, not yet commercialised.
markets: Pre-revenue; headquarters in Paris with hubs in New York, Montreal and Singapore; plans healthcare work with Nabla before broader commercialisation.
rationale: High-profile European AI lab, but pre-revenue with no product to market yet; weak F1 fit for now.

name: Ineffable Intelligence
desc: AI research lab founded by David Silver building reinforcement-learning systems that learn from their own experience.
markets: Pre-revenue research lab in London; no products, customers or international operations disclosed.
rationale: Research-stage lab with no product or brand to market; weak F1 fit.

name: Xanadu Quantum Technologies
desc: Builds photonic quantum computers and the PennyLane quantum software library for industry, research and government users.
markets: Customers and partners include Lockheed Martin, AMD, US Air Force Research Laboratory, Rolls-Royce, Volkswagen and Mitsubishi Chemical; Canadian government programmes.
rationale: Newly listed quantum company with partners in automotive and aerospace; F1 could showcase computing technology and support investor visibility.
changed: Listed in March 2026 through SPAC merger with Crane Harbor Acquisition Corp

name: EliseAI
desc: Sells conversational AI software that automates leasing, resident communication and patient scheduling for apartment operators and clinics.
markets: Customers are US apartment owners and outpatient practices; one team in Toronto; no verified customers or expansion plans outside the US.
rationale: US-focused B2B software for landlords and clinics with little consumer marketing; weak to moderate F1 fit.

name: Enveda
desc: Clinical-stage biotech using machine learning and chemistry to develop medicines from natural molecules for eczema, asthma and metabolic disease.
markets: Pre-revenue; drug candidates in clinical trials, run from Boulder, Colorado; no marketed products or verified international operations.
rationale: Pre-revenue drug developer with no consumer brand or marketed product to promote; weak F1 fit.

name: Oratomic
desc: Start-up developing fault-tolerant neutral-atom quantum computers with efficient error correction, founded in 2026 by Caltech-linked physicists.
markets: Pre-revenue hardware developer in Pasadena, California; no customers or international operations disclosed.
rationale: Pre-revenue quantum hardware start-up with no product or brand to market; weak F1 fit.

name: Oxide Computer Company
desc: Builds rack-scale servers with integrated software for on-premises cloud computing, sold to enterprises, government and national laboratories.
markets: Named customers are US organisations such as Lawrence Livermore and Idaho National Laboratories, CoreSite and Switch; no verified customers abroad.
rationale: Engineering-led hardware brand selling to US enterprises and government; F1 technology tie-in plausible but not obvious.

name: Sigma Computing
desc: Sells cloud analytics and business intelligence software that lets business users analyse data in cloud warehouses through spreadsheets.
markets: Offices in San Francisco, New York, London and Sydney; EMEA headquarters in London with stated plans to expand across EMEA.
rationale: Growing enterprise analytics brand; rivals Alteryx and Salesforce sponsor F1, so data storytelling and B2B hospitality fit.

name: Wonderful
desc: Provides an enterprise platform for customer-facing AI agents across voice, chat and email, deployed with local teams.
markets: Deployments in more than 30 countries across Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and Latin America; engineering in Israel.
rationale: Fast-growing enterprise AI brand selling to telecoms and banks across regions; F1 hospitality and technology showcase fit its markets.

name: Zelostech (Zelos Technology)
desc: Makes and operates driverless electric delivery vans for logistics customers such as DHL and Singapore Post.
markets: Vehicles in China and Singapore; Malaysia road trials; company claims 20+ countries; expansion in South-East Asia and Middle East planned.
rationale: Autonomous-vehicle maker expanding across Asia and the Middle East; F1 technology showcase plausible, not obvious.
